design_condition: Two offset volumes flank the boulevard, preserving generous open space in front and three planted open spaces toward the track field, while partly failing to connect directly to the viaduct side.

positive.statement: The very clear and controlled urban planning creates a well-sized and easy-to-read statement.

position.rationale: Top view clearly shows two offset compact volumes and generous open space between and around them.

positive.statement: The access structure is clear, concise, flexible, and implemented in an exemplary manner.

position.rationale: The front volume and its repeated openings provide the clearest approximate anchor for the access structure.

positive.statement: The ground-floor uses are intelligently placed and support attractive connections with the outside space.

position.rationale: Ground-level frontage of the larger southwest volume anchors connections between interior uses and external open space.

positive.statement: The project promises to be economical and sustainable because of its simple volumes.

position.rationale: Economy and sustainability are global judgments about the simple massing, without a single spatial referent.

negative.statement: Direct access from the viaduct side is missing, despite being easy to implement.

position.rationale: A perimeter location beside the offset volumes approximates the unresolved viaduct-side ground access.

negative.statement: The space under the viaduct is undefined and insufficiently convincing, with required connections and parking provisions unresolved.

position.rationale: The model does not distinguish viaduct infrastructure; this marks a plausible edge zone for unresolved connections and parking.

negative.statement: The access system becomes mechanical and repetitive because the upper-floor sequence lacks spatial weighting.

position.rationale: Upper levels of the larger volume provide an approximate anchor for the repetitive access sequence.

negative.statement: Many essential spatial relationships are not maintained, making the flow of people and goods and orientation more difficult.

position.rationale: The whole connected arrangement is relevant, but internal relationships are not directly separable in the exterior sample.

negative.statement: The long internal paths and weak connection of the entrance hall to public uses require special functional attention.

position.rationale: The southwest ground-floor edge is a plausible constrained anchor for the entrance hall and public-use connection.

negative.statement: The narrow inner courtyards provide only limited daylight to adjacent rooms.

position.rationale: Two narrow voids are visible within the northeast volume footprint, supporting the courtyard daylight concern.

negative.statement: The high proportion of glass is likely to have a negative impact on the energy balance.

position.rationale: A broad southwest-facing envelope anchor represents the stated glass proportion, though materials are not distinguished.
